A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniLight, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including figures, tables, equations, and references. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; the separately referenced supplementary material is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval scores, token and spherical-harmonics ablations, directional-sensitivity analysis, and qualitative generation and relighting results in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen3-VL comparisons, quantitative HDR-rendering results, and a directional-relighting comparison.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a separate multi-exposure reconstruction model to extend LDR generation to HDR. Section 5.4 revises the stated relighting inputs from albedo, normals, roughness, and metallicity to depth, normals, and albedo with zeroed irradiance. The core encoders, embedding architecture, and contrastive/SH objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation from LDR environment-map generation to HDR lighting estimation assessed through object renders (Table 2 and Figure 10). The original indoor/outdoor coverage and 8,020-map dataset remain. Newly named relighting-training sources are additional disclosures, not proof that those sources were introduced after v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-VL 2B to the retrieval comparison in Table 1 and Qwen3-VL embeddings to the relighting comparison in Figure 12. CLIP and the existing generation/relighting comparators remain. Table 2 evaluates the already-used DiffusionLight-Turbo on the added HDR-rendering task.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes the reported crop sampling from random horizontal rotations to fixed 40-degree intervals; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. V2 adds six HDR-rendering metrics and a relighting sweep in 60-degree intervals. The 603-entry retrieval evaluation and existing 30-degree latent-similarity sweep remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 12 tests whether relighting responds appropriately to environment-map rotations, comparing UniLight with Qwen3-VL on indoor and outdoor examples. The existing token/SH ablations, SH reconstructions, and latent directional-sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions show the same two generation seeds in Figure 9. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v2's new table and qualitative comparison do not introduce such reporting.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands results beyond the existing retrieval evidence: it adds quantitative HDR-rendering evaluation, Qwen3-VL retrieval scores, and directional-relighting findings. New Table 2 reports UniLight/DiffusionLight-Turbo PSNR of 28.85/27.77 and LPIPS of 0.079/0.088. Table 1 adds Qwen3-VL R@1 of 8.9 and MRR of 0.179. Existing retrieval and ablation values are unchanged; these additions are not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The embedding formulation, SH supervision, and combined loss are mathematically unchanged. Renaming the contrastive loss to LC and making the total-loss equation inline are notation/layout edits. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified lighting embedding, contrastive alignment, directional SH supervision, and usefulness for retrieval, environment-map generation, and relighting. New experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly contrasts general-semantic Qwen3-VL embeddings with lighting-specific embeddings, interpreting weak responses to rotation as a limitation for precise lighting control. The existing explanations of text ambiguity and limitations concerning spatially varying illumination remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 newly documents two-stage relighting training, InteriorVerse/Hypersim plus synthetic and real training sources, SD 3.5 Medium, and zeroed irradiance. These disclosures do not establish that the training procedure changed. Conversely, v1's explicit sky-replacement instruction is shortened. The project URL is merely relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to BLIP-2 and MetaQueries for learnable queries, Qwen3-VL for comparisons, and Hypersim/InteriorVerse for training data. The related-work narrative and overall positioning remain largely intact. Consolidating duplicate LightLab references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted prose reductions and terminology corrections, expands Sections 5.3–5.4, and adds acknowledgments. The seven-section organization and most explanatory text remain, without a substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 2 and Figures 10 and 12, expands Table 1, updates pipeline diagrams, and relocates existing displays. Figure 5's caption correctly identifies recall and rank metrics instead of cosine similarity. V1's relighting Figure 10 is retained as Figure 11; most visual material remains.

improvement.justification: The added Qwen3-VL comparisons and quantitative HDR-rendering results strengthen evidence for the representation's practical usefulness. Corrected metric labels and clearer relighting-training documentation also improve interpretation and reproducibility. The overall gain is limited because the HDR reconstruction and evaluation protocol remain sparsely specified, while the central method and existing results are unchanged.
